blocks.explanation:
The signs repeat in the pattern \(+,\ +,\ -\), so the series itself is not an A.P.
But \(3n\) terms make exactly \(n\) groups of three.
Plan: add each group; the group sums form an A.P. of \(n\) terms; sum that A.P.
steps:
Given: \(3 + 5 - 7 + 9 + 11 - 13 + \dots\) to \(3n\) terms.
To find: the sum.
Method: Ignoring signs, the numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, ... go up by 2. Group the terms in threes, \((3 + 5 - 7) + (9 + 11 - 13) + \dots\); there are \(3n \div 3 = n\) groups.

Add each group
\[3 + 5 - 7 = 1\]
\[9 + 11 - 13 = 7\]
\[15 + 17 - 19 = 13\]
Why: Working out the first few groups shows the pattern of the group sums.

The group sums form an A.P.
\[1,\ 7,\ 13,\ \dots\]
\[a_1 = 1,\quad d = 6,\quad n \text{ terms}\]
Why: Each group's numbers are 6 more than the previous group's (three steps of 2), so each group sum is \(6 + 6 - 6 = 6\) more.

Check with \(n = 2\) (6 terms)
\[3 + 5 - 7 + 9 + 11 - 13 = 8\]
\[2(3 \cdot 2 - 2) = 2 \times 4 = 8 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula agrees with direct addition.

blocks.explanation:
Same idea as part (i): signs \(+,\ +,\ -\) repeat, so group the terms in threes.
\(3n\) terms give \(n\) groups.
Plan: find the group sums, see that they form an A.P., and add \(n\) of them.
steps:
Given: \(1 + 4 - 7 + 10 + 13 - 16 + \dots\) to \(3n\) terms.
To find: the sum.
Method: Without signs the numbers 1, 4, 7, 10, ... go up by 3. Group in threes: \((1 + 4 - 7) + (10 + 13 - 16) + \dots\), \(n\) groups.

Add each group
\[1 + 4 - 7 = -2\]
\[10 + 13 - 16 = 7\]
\[19 + 22 - 25 = 16\]
Why: The first few group sums reveal the pattern.

The group sums form an A.P.
\[-2,\ 7,\ 16,\ \dots\]
\[a_1 = -2,\quad d = 9,\quad n \text{ terms}\]
Why: Each group's numbers are 9 more than the previous group's (three steps of 3), so each group sum is \(9 + 9 - 9 = 9\) more.

Check with \(n = 2\) (6 terms)
\[1 + 4 - 7 + 10 + 13 - 16 = 5\]
\[\dfrac{2}{2}(18 - 13) = 5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula agrees with direct addition.
